overview: The Council approved the city's five-year CDBG consolidated plan, authorized land takings for the Brooks Elementary Safe Routes to School project, and affirmed the authorization of use variances. Members also requested comprehensive financial and staffing data to prepare for projected budget shortfalls due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Public Hearing on CDBG Consolidated and Annual Action Plans
items.summary: Approved the 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan and 2020 Annual Action Plan, authorizing the city to apply for $1,574,868 in Community Development Block Grant funds.

items.title: Safe Routes to School Easements and Roadway Alterations
items.summary: Approved an order of taking for 12 permanent and temporary easements to facilitate sidewalk improvements near Brooks Elementary School; the Council also passed a resolution requesting the administration extend the proposed bike lane further down High Street.

items.title: Medford Rental Assistance Program Update
items.summary: Reviewed the status of the CPA-funded rental assistance program and requested a report on the number of resident inquiries received by ABCD and Housing Families.

items.title: Authorization of Use Variances
items.summary: The motion passed to approve a resolution requesting the Zoning Board of Appeals acknowledge that use variances are authorized in Medford based on a 2016 city solicitor opinion.

items.title: Requests for Financial and Staffing Reports
items.summary: Approved joint resolutions requesting a breakdown of public safety staffing levels, vacant positions, snow and ice account balances, and written revenue forecasts; the Council also requested an analysis of the feasibility of municipal bond deficit financing.

items.title: Local Infrastructure and Public Health Resolutions
items.summary: Approved resolutions calling for the repair of 9th Street, a status report on the Tufts Square project, and an update on plans for expanded COVID-19 and antibody testing for residents.

items.title: Recreational Programming and Waste Management Contract
items.summary: Requested the Recreation Department expand socially distanced virtual programming and approved a request to amend the waste management contract to include bulk pickup for Maple Park condominiums.

items.title: Joint Petition for Federal Emergency Financial Relief
items.summary: Approved a joint resolution with the Mayor and School Committee petitioning the federal government for direct financial stimulus to offset municipal revenue losses resulting from the pandemic.

items.title: Committee Reports and Records
items.summary: Tabled three committee reports and approved the records of the May 5, 2020 meeting.
